title: Component tail bounded by total influence
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the product space, and let $k\in\mathbb N$. Then $(k+1)\sum_{S:\,|S|>k}\mathbb E_{x\sim P}[f_S(x)^2]\le I(f)$, where $f_S$ is the $S$-component and $I(f)$ is the total influence.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with positive coordinate weights summing to one
$f$ is real-valued on the product space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $k\in\mathbb N$. Then $(k+1)\sum_{|S|>k}\mathbb E_Pf_S^2\le I(f)$.
